arms.purpose: Prove that local RTT availability cannot manufacture negotiation when the remote SDP lacks a T.140 text media offer.
Prove that a manipulated local-policy negative cannot become negotiated or ready merely because the remote SDP offers T.140.
Positive negotiation control proving that successful T.140 SDP negotiation remains weaker than independently observed T.140 readiness.

requiredFacts: remote T.140 capability is parsed from an m=text section with t140/1000 mapping
local RTT policy is preserved independently from remote capability
answer T.140 acceptance is preserved independently from both
rttNegotiated=true requires local policy + remote T.140 offer + answer acceptance

provesOnly: Baudot can independently classify controlled RTT negotiation/readiness states
remote capability, local policy, SDP negotiation, first text observation, and terminal readiness remain separate evidence facts
successful T.140 negotiation does not itself establish RTT usability
doesNotEstablish: a standards requirement to disable RTT in any session
